I received this today; our dog was hit by a car last month and somehow survived despite head injuries, very lucky. We live in the woods and brush/trees often conceal his whereabouts. This solves that issue, plus a full fence will be going up on our property soon! Although as you can see by the pic he is less than thrilled with wearing it (won't look at me!) I am relieved to have something to make him more visible when we are hiking and also on our property/extra visibility if he does escape towards the road again. It's probably my computer monitor that makes the listing pic look like the vest is simply a yellow orange...it is much more vivid in real life. This thing is BRIGHT. It is true hunter's *neon* orange, and as you can see from the pics attached, the reflective straps are VERY reflective (that's just my cell camera flash in a lighted room). If you are looking for a fashion accessory for your pooch, this is something out of a hunting catalogue not Doggie Vogue but visibility is exactly what I was after. Our dog is about 60 lbs, Border Collie/Springer Spaniel mix, a little on the barrel-chested side...he measures about 33" circumference at the widest spot on his rib cage and a size L fits him perfectly with plenty of room to adjust the straps. I could easily cut the excess strap off but there is about 4" extra around his neck and about 3" extra strap at his waist. So far it appears very well made yet the fabric is nice and light...and as someone whose dog goes nuts listening to crinkly fabric, I can say that this is not crinkly or loud at all. In fact he is now fast asleep wearing it indoors. I'll update the review with wear and tear feedback once we've had it for a few weeks.

Let's start by saying that these Sennheiser headphones are not the best I've ever purchased. Although the leatherette pads create a nice seal to help with noise, they are not comfortable for longer listening sessions. I was mainly interested in the active noise canceling and the aptX wireless for work, and I was pleased to find headphones that looked professional and clean. The mic was also something I was hoping to use for conference calls, but unfortunately, it's omnidirectional, so everyone can hear the whole room around me. This makes it challenging to use in a busier workspace, and it's frustrating because I like the sound, look, and convenience of wireless. I have not found anything else on the market that looks better for under $400, and while there are headsets that could be better for conference calls, they lack aptX or AAC for music listening. Although the newer, more expensive PXC 550 might have a better mic, it's not worth the extra $200. If the mic was better at ignoring background sounds and noises, these headphones would be perfect for me.

This chair has decent lumbar adjustment, but it lacks height adjustment which can be problematic for some users. The mesh back is a nice touch, but the neck support is not very useful and requires an extra allen wrench to adjust properly. Even after adjusting, it still didn't feel natural or useful for me. The worst part of the chair was the seat pad, which lacked cushioning and made me feel like I was sitting on a metal plate after just 20-30 minutes. This may not be an issue for smaller users, but for someone my size (6'3" and 215 pounds), it was uncomfortable. I've had other chairs in the past that have worn thin after extended use, but this one was uncomfortable from the start. However, Amazon's customer service was great and they promptly helped me with the return process.

PROS: • Cozy and soft material provides nice cushion for comfortable sleep • Top strap allows for easy attachment to backpack or luggage, eliminating one less thing to carry during trips • Adjustable chin support tails stabilizes the chin by wrapping around the whole neck, nestling the head, and preventing facial drooping that disrupts a peaceful sleep • Adjustable chin support tails allows the head to lean comfortably on either side, either by placing the left tail on top to lean left or the right tail on top to lean right • Adjustable for chin support by wrapping around the neck or as a side pillow to lay on by folding it in half • Back support does not push your head forward, unlike other travel pillows CONS: • Stuff material occupies a lot of real estate if placed in storage like a backpack • Has a tendency to feel like the pillow is constrictive if improperly wrapped around the neck • No velcro attachment on chin support tails, therefore it has a tendency to slowly expand over-time, thereby loosening its secure wrapping around the neck and support for the head, and allowing facial drooping, resulting in an uncomfortable rest • No breathable ventilation holes, so has a tendency to become warm if sweaty or air temperature is warm

I'm a big fan of cast iron cookware and have a collection of pieces from various companies, old and new. I wanted to add a cast iron baking pan to my collection, but unfortunately, Lodge doesn't make one and there aren't many options out there. So, I decided to try this one out. 

My first impression was that it was okay, but upon further inspection, the quality was not up to par with Lodge or Griswold. The casting was rough and unfinished, and the pan was covered in an unacceptable amount of black gunk. I had to spend an hour hand sanding it down to bare metal, and even then, there was still a lot of questionable material that came off. After seasoning it, it was finally safe to use. 

If you do decide to purchase this pan, be prepared for a lot of work. Wear old clothes and rubber gloves because you will end up covered in gunk when sanding it down. In hindsight, it really depends on how much work you're willing to put into it and the original cost. I would have given it more stars if it was ready to use out of the box and finished better.

So, I bought the Keracolor Copper conditioner hoping to give my dishwater blonde hair a reddish tint. I followed the instructions and mixed it with my regular conditioner, but even after leaving it on for 10 minutes, I saw no results. Then, I tried using the Keracolor conditioner alone for 10 minutes and still saw no change. Finally, I left it in for 30 minutes and saw a slight reddish sheen when light hit my hair, but it was barely noticeable. I think this product works better on hair that has been previously treated, as it makes the hair more porous and easier to absorb the color. As for me, I have virgin hair, so that may have affected the outcome. The conditioner did make my hair feel great and it looked shiny after use, but unfortunately, I have dandruff and found myself scratching my head a lot, resulting in the tips of my nails being dyed copper. The color doesn't wash out easily either. I will use it once a week to maintain my hair color, but I don't plan on buying it again.

Let me start by saying that I have Lutron Caseta installed all over my house and have been using it for months. The reliability of automation and connectivity for Lutron is top-notch compared to this manufacturer. I was hoping to integrate this device with HomeKit automation for my lights, but unfortunately, it's not ready for prime time yet.

First of all, pairing the device is very sporadic. Sometimes the device presents itself to be paired, while other times it doesn't. I tried pairing it on multiple devices, different iPhones and iPads, but it didn't work. Secondly, device updates are very delayed and can take up to 10-15 minutes, which is unacceptable for a sensor that should operate in near real-time. I'm not sure what the issue is, but it's definitely a problem.

Lastly, automation in HomeKit is unreliable. I set up a simple routine where the lights turn on when the sensor detects motion, but half the time, it wouldn't trigger the automation routine at all. Other times, there was a significant delay in triggering the lights, ranging from 10 seconds to a minute. This defeats the purpose of having automation, and I might as well turn the lights on manually. I'm pretty sure the issue is with this manufacturer and not HomeKit. With my Lutron set-up, there's almost no lag time when I turn on the lights through the HomeKit app, and it's 100% reliable.

In conclusion, I wouldn't recommend this device for anyone looking to integrate it with their HomeKit automation. The pairing is sporadic, the device updates are delayed, and the automation is unreliable. Stick with Lutron Caseta for a more reliable and seamless experience.

Before I purchased these I asked the seller how to select the "boy" set with the Pokemon toys inside, since that is not an option. I was assured that I was receiving the Pokemon set. Overall I've liked this set over the past few years but it has a few serious design flaws which for me meant that I had to reassemble it using a heavy helping of blue threadlocker after it fell apart in my bag. As a bonus I only managed to lose one of the washers! -The lock washers that are used to hold the thing together are the cut washer type which from an engineering standpoint literally do nothing once everything has been tightened. I supposed they could help in light of the next design flaw I will mention but in my case they didn't. It's truly astonishing that manufacturers have ever used these types of lock washers and completely insane that they continue to do so. -The rods that threads through each end and are responsible for tying all the individual tools together are about 1/4" too short. This means that when you tighten it down you don't tighten against the rod, you tighten against all of the tools. The effect of this is that you can't really tighten them down an effective amount because the individual tools won't be able to swing out. They did put a small dab of blue threadlocker on it but it wasn't enough to prevent mine from falling apart. I suggest that anyone who buys this disassembles it and puts a healthy helping of blue or maybe even red threadlocker on the threads. Once applying a bunch of threadlocker it seems to stay together enough for infrequent use. If you are someone who only has this for emergencies then I consider it a worthwhile tool for your pack. If you are planning on using this frequently then I suggest looking elsewhere. I see a lot of complaints about rust but unfortunately that is the nature of things. Stainless would be too heavy (and softer), aluminum would be too soft, and titanium would be too expensive. I suppose there could be a better coating on it but in the end you just need to not let it sit around wet. Keeping it slightly oiled would also help.

An item this heavy needs proper packing, because it's going to get rough treatment during shipping. Mine arrived with one bent corner on the backsplash, and the legs loose and rolling around inside the box. That might have caused the small ding in the table surface, which already shows signs of rust. We put something on it to prevent water from beading there and have crossed our fingers. We bought it to use outside in a semi-protected area, and keep it covered when not in use. The adjustable shelf is handy. It has a "front" and back, so if you're particular, be sure to look for the brand name and put it where you want it. It is a good height for working under normal conditions (food prep, etc.). However, our countertop grill is 8" tall, making the surface a little high for true comfort. The legs would be fairly easy to shorten with a metal cutting blade and a lot of elbow grease, but it would need to be done BEFORE assembly. Cut the TOPS of the legs, which fit into sleeves on the table top. Then assemble the shelf, and the adjustable feet can be leveled as necessary once you get it in place. Also, if you have a mind to put locking casters on the table, the additional height should be taken into account before assembling the table, if you want a particular working height.

I was searchin' for a smoker like my son's swanky Bradley with the automatic smoke maker. I stumbled upon this lil' thing instead. I combined it with a Masterbuilt Sportsman Elite smoker, and now I got somethin' like the Bradley but at half the price. What's cool about this gizmo is that you can really do some cold smokin'. Just hook it up to your smoker with a 3" flex dryer vent, and the smoke maker will be a few feet away from the smoker. By the time the smoke reaches the smoker, it's about the same temp as the air outside. In fact, I smoked some cheese the other day, and the temp inside was just 35 degrees -- almost the same as the outside temp.

Another plus is that it uses regular wood chips, which are way cheaper and easier to find than those fancy Bradley wood biscuits. The only downside I've had with this is that you gotta check on the wood chips in the chip holder now and then. Cuz of how it's designed, the chips are in a column right above the heating element. The idea is that as the chips burn, the ones above keep fallin' onto the heating element, turn to ash (which falls into the ash pan) and then get replaced by the ones above. In reality, sometimes the chips above stick together and don't fall on the heating element. You know when this happens because the smoke coming out is super light.

The way to fix this is to take somethin' like a long screwdriver or knife and poke the chips in the holder, breakin' the jam and lettin' them feed right. This is one area where the Bradley is better designed and doesn't have this problem. But with a lil' bit of manual effort, you can have a versatile smoke maker at a much lower cost.

Alright, so this cable is like one of those super thicc cables you see everywhere. But guess what? Thicker doesn't mean better quality. I've used thinner cables and they're way less annoying to work with. This thick cable and its bulky plug just won't fit in the pocket of my Vizio M Series TV or next to any other HDMI cable in my Sony ES receiver. So, let me tell you the real deal about HDMI cables: they either work or they don't. There's no such thing as a "premium" passive cable.

There are only 3 possible outcomes with HDMI cables: 1. Doesn't work 2. Works but with weird artifacts (like random white dots) 3. Works perfectly. If you get 1 or 2, your equipment just doesn't like the cable, or maybe you need an active cable for a long run. If you get 3, you're all set. There's no higher quality than "works" because of how HDMI signals are transmitted with error correction and all that digital stuff.

So, that's a long way of saying this cable is just too thick for no reason. Thicker doesn't mean more "premium," it just means harder to use. Or, in my case, completely useless. The last couple of Amazon Basics HDMI cables I got were normal thickness and had normal sized connectors, and they worked just fine. C'mon, Amazon! Stop with the thick cable madness!

I perpetually have lots of yellow post-it notes by my desk and organization of these important notes is always a challenge. I love the idea of Rocketbook (it can scan your notes which are written in the Rocketbook and send them to the cloud so you never lose the notes and you can stay organized). My criticism of the Rocketbook is that scanning from the iPhone app isn't so easy. It will literally take 30-60 seconds for the app to register the note and then scan it. It is very important to have good lighting, but even with good lighting it isn't a simple snap of your camera. for the 30-60 seconds (and it is closer to 60 seconds if not more), you need to keep steady but at the same time move the phone ever so slightly until the app detects the note. It is a little bit of a hassle and not quick or easy. The rest of the stuff is good. I opened multiple folders on my cloud service- one for important #'s, one for file notes, one for personal notes, etc, and you can designate which folder you want a note to scan to. I love that. The pen it comes with, a frixion .7mm pen is just okay. This is my personal preference. I prefer a wider, darker pen and this is a pretty fine point. Overall, this is a great idea, but with the two exceptions noted here.

The appearance of this pen is quite sleek, with a unique color that really makes it stand out. The sections of the pen fit together nice and tight, and the grip is smooth but still offers good traction when you're writing. The logo isn't too flashy, as it's only in one spot, and the overall shape is a bit different from other fountain pens I have, with the cap and body being more similar. 

As for how it writes, it's pretty consistent and the weight is just right for using it for longer periods of time. I haven't had any problems with skipping or anything like that. The only small downside I've noticed is that it can be a bit scratchy on cheaper paper, like regular printer paper, compared to other fountain pens I have at this price range. On better quality paper, though, it writes really smoothly. The cap posts well and doesn't add too much extra weight that would throw off the writing experience, and it still gives a satisfying "click" when you put it on to protect the nib. I used this pen every day at work before I got more pens and colors, and I've been trying to work it back into my weekly rotation.

In terms of accessories, the converter it comes with is a bladder type, which is a bit unusual for a pen at this price point. I haven't had any issues with it leaking or anything like that, and it's nice that it's included when you buy the pen. 

To sum it up, this is a really great starter fountain pen that's perfect for everyday writing, and it even lets you try out different ink choices right from the get-go.

I have just received the knife so the four stars for sturdiness are based on appearances which I know can be deceiving sometimes. The knife arrived earlier than anticipated and in perfect condition. I wasn’t sure what the finish would look like based on their own description of the treating process but the one I got is really well done with no blemishes. I watched some reviews where people thought the blade had corrosion already on it out of the box. Is not corrosion just the treatment process. I tested the sharpness on some paper and found the main cutting edge to be not quite as sharp as the other two which are scary sharp. A few seconds on my ceramic sticks and leather strop and the main blade was equal to the others so no complaints there. The sheath seems to be decent quality and has excellent retention with no rattle so I’m really happy about that. It kinda helps with the perception of quality however the giant mercenary tactical banner on the blade somewhat negates that if that makes any sense. As far as durability I really don’t plan on abusing it to find out so I really can’t comment. I honestly bought it because the reviews are good and I like the looks of it aside from the aforementioned logo. The knife Is definitely mini in size but fits my smaller hands well. Oh and the magnetic box closure is kinda neat as I’m pretty easily amused. YouTube has some decent review videos if you want to check it out before purchase. I know I did.

When it comes to expectations, ya really gotta keep in mind what ya payin' for, or else ya might end up feelin' let down. From afar, the thing looks pretty alright and does what it's supposed to. I bought this to fill a gap till I can get my hands on somethin' a lil' more fancy. For the price I paid, it ain't too shabby. I almost got it from another place for double the price - thank the heavens I checked Amazon first! If I'd paid more, I'd be fumin'. 

The veneer on this thing came cracked in three parts, with two of 'em smack dab on the front of one of the doors, and it ain't easy to miss. There were also some scrapes and marks when it showed up - check out the pics. The doors got this cheapo plastic stuff for hardware, which I already had to super glue back together. The feet ain't much better - more cheap plastic and they ain't easy on the eyes, but at least they're kinda hidden. We'll see how long this thing lasts, and I'll try to update y'all. 

Update: Welp, it's only been a month, and I'm already on the hunt for a replacement. This thing picks up scratches like nobody's business, and the dark color makes 'em stand out like a sore thumb. One of the shelves is startin' to sag from the stuff I put in there, and it ain't even that heavy. Guess this thing's really only meant for shoes or somethin'.

Appearance: It looks quite streamlined, though the color is fairly unique so it stands out. The pen sections fit together quite snugly and the smooth grip provides some good traction despite its smoothness. The logo is only in one location so it's not gaudy. The overall shape is different from my other fountain pens insomuch as both the cap and body are quite similar rather than the cap being markedly different. Function: It writes very consistently and it's weight allows it to be used for longer periods of time. I've also not had any skips or similar issues. The only minor negative thing I have to say is that it's scratchier on cheaper paper (e.g. run of the mill printer type) than the other fountain pens I have at this price point. On decent quality paper, it writes quite smoothly. The cap posts well while not added that much additional weight as to throw off the writing experience. It also still yields a satisfying "click" when protecting the nib. I used it every day at work before acquiring more pens and colors, though I am working it back into my weekly rotation. Accessories: The converter is a bladder type which is atypical at this price point. I've not had any issues with it leaking or anything. Its inclusion with the purchase of the pen is nice. Conclusion: This is a great starter fountain pen suitable for everyday writing that even allows you to conveniently expand upon your ink choices from the outset.

These headphones sound absolutely amazing. Better than anything I've ever heard. Supposedly, they are the best closed back headphones you can get at this price range. And I am inclined to believe that. They come with a leather (possibly real) carrying bag, a comically long straight cord, and an annoyingly sized spiral cord. The spiral cord went down to my knees with my music player in my pocket, making it not ideal for commuting. I purchased a much shorter cord for my commute for around $10. Very impressed overall. However, these broke on me after 3 and a half months of use. I took them off and SNAP, a piece of the hinge on my left side snapped, leaving wires exposed and the headphones unwearable (they still work). Throughout my ownership of these cans, whenever I moved the ear cups, there was a cracking sound, like the plastic was screaming for help. I thought that this was just an odd feature, but I now believe it to be a design or manufacturing flaw. I am unsure if Audio Technica and/or Amazon would cover this under a warranty or not. I do not have the budget to pay them to fix it, buy new headphones, or waste money shipping the headphones back and forth to possibly get a free repair done. So, I will probably have to do a crappy epoxy or tape job to fix these, as I absolutely cannot stand to listen to dollar store ear buds anymore. I bought these headphones not only because of the sound, but because I was led to believe that these were extremely durable headphones that would last me years to come. That is perfect, because I used these on my daily commute, brought them camping, took them halfway across the US with me, and I used them for practicing my instruments. But alas, they did not last, so I cannot recommend these headphones with their current build quality, unless you are to only use them at your desk. And at that point, you might as well buy more expensive, better sounding headphones (not that these sound bad, because they don't). I am impressed, but at the same time thoroughly disappointed in this product. I cannot recommend these to your average consumer. Consume at your own risk.

So our dog survived being hit by a car last month, and we were looking for a way to make him more visible when we are hiking or he is on our property. We live in the woods, and it's easy for brush and trees to conceal him. This vest solves that problem. We're also planning to put up a fence around our property, but in the meantime, this vest provides extra visibility if he does escape towards the road again. The vest is very bright, and the reflective straps are very reflective. It's not a fashion accessory for your pooch, but it's exactly what we were looking for. Our dog is a Border Collie/Springer Spaniel mix, about 60 lbs, and a little on the barrel-chested side. He measures about 33" circumference at the widest spot on his rib cage, and a size L fits him perfectly with plenty of room to adjust the straps. There's about 4" extra around his neck and about 3" extra strap at his waist, but we could easily cut the excess strap off. The fabric is nice and light, and it's not crinkly or loud at all. Our dog is now fast asleep wearing it indoors. We'll update the review with wear and tear feedback once we've had it for a few weeks.

Let me start by saying that Karin Slaughter is one of my absolute favorite authors. Her storytelling abilities are unparalleled. However, I must admit that I was a bit disappointed with Criminal. Don't get me wrong, the writing itself was great, but I found the constant jumping back and forth between the present and past to be a bit confusing. It wasn't until much later in the book that it became clear why this was happening. At one point, I almost gave up on the book entirely. But I persevered because, well, it's Karin Slaughter! And I'm glad I did because the story really picked up in the second half. 

That being said, there were still a few things that bothered me. For example, the idea that a group of young girls were virgins simply because they had a box of tampons among their belongings was absurd. Anyone who knows anything about tampons knows that they don't have anything to do with virginity. But I digress. Once the story finally started to come together, I found it to be a thrilling, engaging read. I couldn't put it down! 

There's also a bonus short story called Snatched at the end of the book, and it was fantastic. Classic Karin Slaughter brilliance. Overall, I enjoyed Criminal despite its somewhat confusing beginning and a few quirks along the way. I would definitely recommend it to anyone who is a fan of the author or the genre. And of course, I'll continue to read Karin Slaughter's books. I'm looking forward to seeing more of Will Trent in future cases!

Update - the third shelf arrived the next day I only received two shelves instead of the 3 I paid for. I have Lutron Caseta throughout the house and have been running it for months - the automation / connectivity reliability for Lutron is rock solid in comparison to this manufacturer - was looking to integrate this device with HomeKit automation of my lights. This is not ready for prime time: 1. Pairing is sporadic. Device is active, but sometimes presents itself to be paired, other times not. Attempted pairing on multiple devices, different iPhones and iPads thinking maybe it was just my iPhone, it wasn't. 2. Device updates are very delayed / latent - as in minutes, sometimes as much as 10-15 minutes. This is supposed to be a sensor that operates in near real time, not sure what the deal is? 3. Automation in Homekit is unreliable. Set up a very simple routine, when it senses movement, turn on the lights. The sensor would blip that it picked up motion - half the time, it would not trigger the automation routine at all. Other times, the latency to trigger the lights would range from 10 seconds to as much as a minute. What's the purpose of that? I'll just turn the lights on manually if it's going to take THAT long. This can't be with Homekit, it's got to be with this manufacturer. With my Lutron set-up, when I turn on the lights through the Homekit app, theres almost imperceptible lag time and 100% reliability to trigger actions, as it should be.

So, I got this big ol' beach chair, right? It's a bit taller than most of them other chairs, which makes it easier for me to get up from it. I was in need of a big humidifier, and it was a plus that it had an essential oil diffuser too. Good things: The item does what it says, making a good strong mist without leaving any residue or white stuff. It goes for around 9-10 hours on max with full water. Since it uses lots of water, you need to add more oil to smell it in the room. I began with 6-8 drops, but ended up using 14-16 drops. The motor is super quiet and the auto-shut off works like it should.

Not-so-good things: The blue light on the dial is pretty bright, and there isn't a way to turn it off. It turns red when it's out of water, but it's still really bright. To fill the water tank, you have to lift it off the base and it usually spills some water. I bet with practice I'd get better, but a top-fill model might be easier. Also, even though the vaporizer motor is almost silent, there is a gurgle and bubble sound now and then as water moves from the tank to the humidifier. It's a spring loaded cap, and I could hear it while trying to fall asleep.

I'm gonna return this unit, but only because of the light and the water tank situation. It works great as a humidifier, but I need a dark, quiet room to sleep.

Okay so I dont know what the heck are all those reviews saying the shoes are good. I've been wanting these shoes for MONTHS; I've been doing my research, going back and forth from Keen, Chacos, Teva, etc. and these shoes had the best reviews every saying they were amazing right... wrong (Trump's voice). I ordered half a size bigger - great choice because even at that the shoe was tight. First hour at work, I had a blisters all over my heels. Second hour at work, I slipped on DRY rocks while cleaning aquarium. Third hour, I slipped on a teeny weeny itty bitty bit of water while carrying an 8 foot ladder. - not pretty at all. I had to actually take off the shoes to be able to go up and down ladders safely. I was so excited for this product but see ya never Teva. Wouldn't recommend this shoe if you are planning to get even a drop of water in front of your path.

Inexpensive and disposable. The tint was what I liked most about them. They are very dark for safety eyewear and that is what I was looking for. The fit was perfect for me snug, but not pinching they stay on top of your head when you need to move them up for a break. The style is comfortable, they didn't hit my cheek, didn't dig into my nose and didn't fog during work. Very lightweight. They look more like sunglasses than safety glasses which is cool. The lenses had a bit of a swirl/distortion near the bottom edge but I ignored given the price. Now the bad part.. They don't last. These are one time use glasses. Like, the kind you have on hand for visitors to your work area. Each pair had a hairline crack on the bridge/nose piece right out of the wrapper. The longest use I was able to get out of a pair is 3 days. It happens suddenly. On the job, go to put them on and snap, right in the middle. I was really excited to find these pop-up tinsel trees online since I haven't seen them in stores this year. I ordered three and they arrived quickly, which was great. My wife thought this was the cutest little thing she’d seen. She wanted it mainly for the harness and leash. Unfortunately because of the way the straps are designed it doesn’t work all that well for that part. The chest buckle is way too low which I didn’t notice when I was ordering it. If you were to actually try to use this on a child as a harness it’s not very secure and slips way up if they’re tugging on it at all. It would have been much better if the chest strap had been adjustable up and down. One idea I had was adding a strap all the way across that attaches to the pack instead of the shoulder pads and comes across under his armpits. But that’s a lot of work to make it useable. I was really excited to read this biography since I'm a big fan of Herbert Marshall's movies and wanted to learn more about him. However, I was disappointed because the book reads more like a long list of his work rather than an in-depth exploration of the man himself. I wanted to know more about his personal relationships, particularly since he was married four times, but the book barely touches on this subject. It doesn't delve into why his marriages ended or explore his alcoholism in any meaningful way. The proof-reading is also pretty bad, with missing words, misused punctuation, and poorly constructed sentences. It was frustrating to read and made it hard to understand some parts of the book. I was expecting a more personal biography, like the one I read about Barbara La Marr, which was much clearer and easier to read. On the plus side, there are a lot of photos, which I always enjoy in a biography. But overall, I don't think this book is worth the $28.00 price tag for a paperback.

I recently bought two packages of these dish towels, each containing a dozen towels. I was excited to use them after reading the reviews and details provided online. However, after washing them and double rinsing them, I was disappointed with the results. The amount of lint left on my washing machine filter was unbelievable, and the same goes for my dryer filter. After drying them thoroughly, I tested them out, and to my dismay, they were not absorbent at all. In fact, I would classify them as non-absorbent or repellent. When I tried to dry my dishes and glasses with them, they were still wet and covered with lint and fibers both inside and outside of the glass. It was like using a synthetic or plastic cloth. I had to use an old dish towel from my collection to dry the glass and dish off, and it worked much better than the new ones. I am extremely dissatisfied with these towels, and I wanted to return them for a full refund. Unfortunately, I was informed that I missed the 30-day return policy. The second package is still unused and unopened, and I cannot give it as a gift since they are of substandard quality. I would not recommend these towels to anyone who is expecting a soft, absorbent cotton dish towel. I have dish cloths that are over 10 years old, purchased at a discount store, and they are more absorbent than these towels. I am writing this review to prevent other buyers from wasting their money on these towels.

This bottle is awesome! The spray function is so cool and useful, especially when it's hot outside. I live in a really hot place, so I love being able to cool down with just a quick spray. The cap is easy to take off and put back on, and it seems pretty strong. The plastic used for the bottle itself is fine, but the cap could be improved with better quality plastic or a rubbery coating. It looks a little cheap compared to the rest of the bottle. But honestly, I would buy this bottle again just for the spray function. It sprays a nice mist and is perfect for hot days when you don't want to get too sweaty. If you live in a hot place or like spending time outside, this is a great bottle for you. Overall, it's a really functional spray and water bottle for people who like to stay active in hot weather!

This product was quite a hassle to assemble. The person who painted the parts went overboard, making it difficult to put them together before bolting them. It took a soft rubber mallet to drive the legs together to create the two a-frames as initial assembly. It's important to line up the holes for the outer and inner legs before moving on to the next step. The plastic caps for the bottom were also troublesome to slide on since they're made of cheap plastic. Even using a rubber mallet to assemble the a-frame caused damage to some of the ends, which made it even more difficult. The cross rods were also a bit of a challenge since there was so much paint on the tips of the rods that I had to chase them several times before finally assembling the rack. The bottom wire trays were also problematic since mine came with a bent bottom tray, which made it tough to place it in the right position before bolting everything together. The hex key they give you is also worthless, providing no torque to push the screw into the nut/rod ends. I ended up using my power drill and a hex bit to make assembly more tolerable. Overall, what should have taken 7-10 minutes to assemble ended up taking 30 minutes of forcing items to fit together. But what do you expect for $30 bucks? Ha ha.

Can't be upgraded or customized (except blade), sound effects poor, only one control button, doesn't come with instructions. POSITIVES: 1) The blade lights up plenty bright, and seems evenly illuminated. 2) There are many choices of color. 3) The hilt seems sturdy. NEGATIVES: 1) The sound effects are poor. They sound like about a 10-second recording in a continuous loop, except there is a gap in the loop so you can tell where the loop begins and ends. Furthermore, whenever you turn off the lightsaber, it says a word (lightsabers aren't supposed to talk!), and as near as I can tell, the word it says is "SLEEPING." 2) This saber can't be upgraded or customized, other than replacing the blade. 3) The blade is not very strong or thick. You'll need to buy a replacement blade if you want to do any dueling at all. 4) Only one control button to handle all of the myriad functions. 5) No instruction manual! You need instructions in order to use that single button to activate a half a dozen different features. The only place to find instructions is online, at the manufacturer's Facebook page, so if you're not a Facebook user, you're SOL because you'll never figure out on your own how to make ONE SINGLE CONTROL button do all the different functions! RECOMMENDATION: For less money than this, you can find a better lightsaber elsewhere, one with a sturdy blade, more than one control button, and instructions. For a little more money, you can get a much, MUCH better lightsaber elsewhere!

As a retired teacher myself I nominate Jordan Peterson as Teacher of the Year. His book provides excellent insights into the challenges and problems of ordinary people like you and me who are struggling to make sense of the world and to cope with its incidents and trials. That's the first aspect. The second aspect are his plans and procedures which lead to the formulation of effective attitudes and values. This is where the book is so valuable. It opens up a path of hope for people who want their lives to improve and to have meaning. The rules Jordon Peterson outlines make perfect sense once he has finished explaining them - in fact many readers will wonder why they didn't previously see what was staring them in the face. These rules are particularly helpful to young men and women commencing their adult lives. These rules clarify what may have only been perceived dimly or not at all. While reading this book I felt that I as a fallible human being was being reached out by another human being who understands the potential of any of us to make poor decisions as well as good ones. The many incidents that Jordan Peterson describes in his book by way of illustration bring a very human dimension to his work. If you have older children or grandchildren buy a copy of this book for them. You will give them a true investment in their future.

This mechanical pencil is a solid choice for those who prefer a weightier feel to their writing instruments. The metal construction is a plus, but there is one design flaw that users should be aware of. If the pencil is dropped on a hard surface and lands on the writing end, it can break a plastic sleeve inside the barrel. This has happened to me twice, rendering the pencil useless. Despite this flaw, I still prefer the feel of this pencil and have purchased three of them. However, given the higher price point, I would expect a more durable design. One feature I appreciate is the clutch that holds the graphite, which allows me to put the graphite back into the pencil when carrying it in my pocket. Overall, a good choice for those who prioritize heft and balance in their writing instruments, but be aware of the design flaw.

This table is heavy, and it needs proper packing to prevent damage during shipping. Unfortunately, mine arrived with one corner of the backsplash bent and the legs loose and rolling around inside the box. This may have caused the small ding in the table surface, which is already showing signs of rust. We applied a water-resistant coating to it and are hoping for the best. We bought it for outdoor use in a partially protected area and keep it covered when not in use. The adjustable shelf is convenient, but be aware that it has a front and back, so make sure you put it where you want it. The height is suitable for normal use, like food preparation, but it may be a bit high for comfort if you have a countertop grill that is 8" tall. The legs can be shortened with a metal cutting blade, but it must be done before assembly by cutting the tops of the legs that fit into sleeves on the table top. After assembly, you can level the adjustable feet as needed. If you plan to add locking casters, keep in mind that it will increase the height of the table, so adjust accordingly before assembly.

I recently had rotator cuff and bicep repair surgery, and I got this sling as a backup for when my main sling needed washing. I specifically wanted one with snap/buckle closures like the one from the hospital, since it's super easy to put on and take off. I also tried another sling, but it wasn't that great. But this one? I loved it so much that it became my main sling!

The inside is incredibly soft, which is a nice change from the scratchy hospital sling with its rough fabric and seams that chafed and peeled my skin. However, the shoulder pad could be narrower, as it sometimes digs into my neck. I replaced it with a pad from another sling, and now it's perfect.

Adjusting the straps is a breeze, and I even trimmed some of the velcro pieces and rounded the pointy ends to make them shorter and quieter. My arm measures 12", and while the sling was a bit too long, I was able to fold the wrist end back an inch or two and secure it with the velcro pieces.

After a week, my surgeon removed my pillow and said I didn't need it anymore, so I don't use that part of the sling. Once you adjust this thing just right for you, you'll love it!

The only design change I'd like to see is with the wrist strap and buckle. The velcro pieces are sewn on, and if they were removable, I could fold the "cuff" back further since it's too long for my arm. So, I'm taking off a star for that reason. Otherwise, I love it!

I purchased copper. I have "dishwater blonde" hair (aka medium-lightish brown) that kind of has a silvery sheen and I wanted to make it more brown with a reddish tint. I first did a 50/50 mix of this conditioner and my conditioner (like the instructions say you can) and left it on for 10 minutes and saw no results. I then did 100% Keracolor conditioner and left it in for 10 minutes and STILL saw no results. Then, finally, I left the conditioner in for 30 minutes and saw barely noticeable results. The only thing I really can tell is that when light hits my hair, it has a reddish sheen, but that's really it - overall, its the same color. I'll probably use this once a week and leave it in for 30 minutes to maintain the color, but I have no plans to buy it again. I have a feeling this stuff works better on pre-treated hair (as you you've had it actually dyed or bleached), which makes the hair more porous so it absorbs the color better. I have "virgin" hair, so I feel like that has to due with my lack of results. On the positive side, after leaving this stuff in my hair for so long, it looks and feels great! its definitely a good conditioner. Lastly, I have dandruff so I find myself scratching my head a bit, unfortunately. This has resulted in the tips of my fingernails being dyed copper. It doesn't wash out, either.

I've been a satisfied MetroPCS client for a long time, but when I relocated to a place with terrible signal, I had to switch to AT&T. Our phones were pretty ancient, so I needed to find budget-friendly replacements. These phones seemed like a good bargain, so I bought them. However, there are a few points to consider...

1) One of the phones was brand new, but the other one had a SIM card in it, all the protective plastic removed, and was clearly used. There was no damage, but I'm not thrilled since I paid for a "Brand New Phone" and got a used one.

2) All the MetroPCS apps are still there, but they don't work if you're not on Metro. I've disabled as many apps as I could, but you can't remove them all, and some you might wanna keep. For example, I don't have "find my phone," and there's no "voicemail" icon to show when you got a voicemail. The only way to access voicemail is by pressing the "1" on the keypad.

3) The playback volume for media is kinda low - my wife uses hers to watch videos on her Facebook feed, and it's hard to hear them even with the volume maxed out.

In general, I like the phone. If I had known it would be used and would miss some features I wanted because it's unlocked but still a Metro phone, I might've made a different choice. You could decide differently, but at least you know more than "It's a great phone and works with AT&T," which is all the info I had when I bought it.

First, I'll mention the good stuff: These headphones feel pretty comfy on my noggin, and my ears don't get all achy when I wear 'em for a good stretch of time (like an hour or two). The sound ain't too shabby either. I ain't no fancy-pants audiophile, but I can tell when headphones are crummy or alright, and these here are alright.

Now for the not-so-good: The Bluetooth on these things is a mess. There's this big ol' delay (1-2 seconds) that's so bad, I just gave up on using it. I plug 'em in with that USB-C to 1/8" cable instead. Forget about watching movies with Bluetooth on these headphones. And there's a delay when pausing tunes too. Takes a second or two from when I hit pause to when the music actually stops. The noise-cancelling feature ain't much help either, just adds some white noise to the mix.

As for how they're built, well, they ain't top-notch. I've had these headphones for 8 months, and the power button's done gone and broke (it's stuck pushed in, so I can't turn 'em on no more). I wasn't expecting these to be the bee's knees or nothin', but losin' the Bluetooth after 8 months ain't great. The padding's startin' to come off too, just like in the picture.

So, if you're lookin' for a decent pair of wired headphones, these might do the trick. But if you want wireless, you best look elsewhere.

I have purchased four of these recorders in the past, because they work extremely well. The only reason I purchased so many of them was because I'm lazy with transcription and sometimes just opted to buy another recorder rather than transcribe the recordings from a previous recorder. The thing is that I bought the previous four recorders from Walmart, which seems to not sell them anymore. I bought my fifth one from Amazon in September 2018, and now, in December 2018, it has inexplicably gone from working just fine to sounding muffled like everything was recorded from beneath a pillow. The recorder was not damaged in any way. I am quite familiar with the settings, having now owned five of these, and I double, triple, and quadruple checked that the mic setting didn't get changed. No. The recorder just fizzled out after two months. I purchased this through Amazon Prime's fulfillment center, and it seems that their quality checks aren't what they used to be when they first started, as many counterfeit and outlet quality items are being sold as originals. I suspect that's what happened here, because my other four recorders have worked just fine for years, and it looks like I'll be clearing them out to start using them again. Not pleased, Amazon. Buyer beware.

Alright, so I'll start with the bad news. It took me a while to figure out how to get this machine working again. The pressure was too low to get a double shot through, and customer care wasn't very helpful. They seemed more interested in avoiding a warranty claim than actually helping me. Even though it only worked once in a blue moon, they insisted that it was fine. Not cool. 

BUT, I finally got it working again. I bought a new metal filter that doesn't trap water inside, and I started cleaning the drip point in the metal cup with a thumbtack. It's not a solution that customer care suggested, but it worked! So, I'm bumping up my original 1-star rating to 3 stars. 

When the machine is working correctly, it makes great cappuccinos and espresso. It's also easy to clean, which is a huge plus. The sealed metal filters that came with the machine weren't great, but the new design fixed that problem. 

Overall, I'd say the machine is good, but the experience with customer care was not. It's frustrating to have to figure out how to fix something yourself when you've paid good money for it. But, at least I finally got it working again.

Gas spills easily from under lid. Three of us tried using it to verify, open/close lid again and every time it leaked. This is explicitly claimed as "no-spill". We were careful from beginning: (1) filled gas at gas station and verified that no single drop spilled while filling, (2) came home and tried to pour slowly into generator... started slow leaking from under lid. We were scared. Though generator was off... it was leaking few drops where generator usually is. So, we moved 15 ft away and filled into a tall glass and noticed the leak again. We cleaned up carefully, moved further and now, other friends tried... same result. Open/close lid, check twice, try again, same result. We figured this is unusable... Gas leak is Hazardous... fumes themselves are highly flammable. Guess what, returns not accepted on this product because... Gas cans shipping has certain constraints. It is not as simple as put in same box and ship. Safety, liability constraints makes returns more expensive than product itself. When Amazon was not allowing returns online, I could not figure why there is a no-return policy - I thought $ 35+ gone down the drain. However, when I chatted with Amazon.com support - they were understanding and helpful. They explained why shipping is complicated... advised me not to return product, but issued refund.

Make sure you have the holes lined up for outer and inner legs before committing to the next step. Speedtalk Mobile's customer service is absolutely dreadful. I got 4 of these cards for my kiddos, and we only used them for like 2 weeks. Fast forward to a year later, I decided to call their customer service to cancel all 4 cards at once. It took a few minutes to get to a representative, but it was smooth sailing from there – or so I thought. It took about a minute to cancel each line, which was fine. But then, when I tried to cancel the 4th card, the rep was like, "I can only do 3 accounts per call. You will need to call back." (Seriously??? I waited on the phone forever and it would only take him 1 more minute to cancel my last line, but I have to call back?) Okay, fine... if that's their policy.

So I called right back, and guess what – the SAME GUY picked up the line immediately!!!! And I had to go through the whole process of telling him I needed to cancel the line. He hung up on me!!! (Well, so much for them being too busy to spare a minute to deal with me on my first call). I dialed back immediately, and was rewarded with another 15 minutes of boring music.... Just to have the same guy pick up my call again so I could finally cancel my line.

To top it all off, I got an email reminder every 10 minutes for 10 hours telling me to refill my card!!!! What a joke.

I bought this because the picture looks awesome. I had the plumbers install this in my new Jacuzzi bathtub. It looks great. However, I needed three fasteners to tighten the Faucet, shower head, and the handle, but only two were in the box. I contacted the company and Ian got back to me and sent the fastener by express mail. Then, the plumbers and General Contractor installed the tub, caulked and sealed. My wife noticed that there was a hairline leaking in the handle. Called the plumbers. They said, there is a plastic valve inside the handle, but it isn't standard, so they could not fix it and just put the valve back and asked me to have the company send me a replacement part. Contacted Ian at the company again and requested the valve. Ian sends me the valve hassle free. The part arrived by express mail again. This time, I personally shut the main water supply to the house and disassembled the handle and switched out the leaking valve...in the process, the handle is slightly misaligned, but it is actually economically better for usage. Turn the main water supply to the house, No leaking. Problem solved. Now, we have beautiful functional Jacuzzi bathtub with great aesthetically pleasing chrome faucet, shower head and ergonomically positioned handle. Great customer service from Ian. I would have given 5 stars, but I had to pay extra for the plumbers to problem solve the leaking valve in the handle, so have to be honest and take a star off. Otherwise, this is a great product, but the factory/manufacturers need better quality assurance program/process improvement in their inventory management. In closing, we really like this product.

My young brother/sister Great Danes have their inner clock all set: at 10 pm most nights, their second wind kicks in. One gets a toy from their toy box and encourages the other to try to take it away. Before you know it, it's an all out free for all in the living room! Rugs go sliding across the room -- even the one that is held down by a couple of sofa legs, doesn't stand a chance. I know they are having fun and don't have the heart to curtail their antics -- but it was becoming tiresome to put the two area rugs back in place most mornings. I wasn't sure that these pads would be good enough to hold them in place, but at the price I thought I'd give it a try. Compared to other products that I have used in the past (without success) these are plump and naturally 'grippy' -- not 'tacky' as some other gripper pads sometimes can be -- and basically don't work anyway. I cut the two pads (easily) to size and waited for a play-night -- that night they went to town. :-) After 20 minutes of hard play - they zonked off to sleep -- and not a rug had budged - even the one that did not have any furniture on it!! I was impressed, to say the least. Will definitely purchase this brand again if ever I need another!

Let me start by saying that I was really excited to get this griddle, but unfortunately, it was a huge disappointment. First off, I should have known to return it after the first use when I realized that anything with a liquid consistency simply slides off into the grease trap. I mean, seriously, who wants a griddle that can't handle scrambled eggs? And to make matters worse, the two plates don't even operate at the same temperature. When I tried to turn down the upper unit to keep pancakes warm, the lower unit stopped cooking altogether and wouldn't readjust until I increased the upper unit to the same temperature. 

But that's not all. After the second use, I noticed two more issues. For one thing, the upper unit doesn't even lie flat on the counter surface, so it's always sloped, even when it's unlocked. I had to readjust it to get it to work properly, which is when I realized that I couldn't even see the dials anymore. 

All in all, I definitely wouldn't recommend this griddle to anyone. Instead, save your money and get the Presto product, which is much cheaper and offers more cooking space. Or, if you really want to splurge, go for an indoor grill or panini press instead. Trust me, you'll be much happier in the end.

First, let's talk about the not-so-good stuff. You can't use this remote to control other devices plugged into the TV, which is kind of a bummer. And the track pad can be, well, a track pad. Now, let me tell you about the good stuff! Plug in the dongle, do a little adjusting with the track pad speed, pick your fave back lighting, and you're good to go. It's like magic!

The size of the keyboard is pretty great too, not too big and not too small. The remote feels light in your hand, but not like it's gonna break or anything. The keys make a nice clicky sound when you type, and it's easy to type on, too. I didn't have any trouble keeping the remote steady while I was typing away.

Now, back to the track pad. It works pretty well most of the time, but sometimes it acts like, well, a track pad. If you're expecting perfection from a track pad, you might wanna lower those expectations a bit. Just sayin'.

The biggest drawback, like I mentioned earlier, is that you can't pair this remote with other devices plugged into your TV. If you've got a fancy smart TV with a not-so-fancy remote, this one's a great choice for under 20 clams. But if you're using a streaming device like a Roku, you're out of luck. You'll still be stuck fat fingering your searches, which is kind of a bummer.

So, overall, this remote's got some great stuff going for it, but it's not perfect. If you're looking for a decent remote for your smart TV and don't need it to control other devices, it's worth checking out. Just remember, the track pad might not always be your best friend.

I got this antenna and mounting pole together, hoping the rotor would help me get better TV signals since I live in a valley. Well, first of all, it arrived as a USED/RETURNED item, not new like it was advertised. And the mounting pole that I paid for wasn't even in the package! So I had to call Amazon customer service, and they didn't even address the fact that the antenna was used and didn't work at first. I figured out it was because the cable provided was bad, so I used my own cable, and now it rotates.

Now, about the mounting pole issue. It was a total mess trying to explain to the customer service rep that I PAID FOR THE POLE when I ordered the antenna. After almost an hour on the phone, they finally agreed to send me the pole "free of charge"... Umm, I already paid for it! It took 2 days to get the antenna, and then an extra week to get the mounting pole.

As for the improved signal? Yeah, not really. I actually get fewer channels now. And if you don't have the antenna mounted where you can see it, you have no idea where it's pointing. So, basically, I'm still searching for a new antenna. Maybe this one works better in a different location, but it didn't do any good in my area. Good luck to anyone trying this out.

We do not have a specific complaint about this product. There is no indication that it is anything other than what it claims to be. After replacing the screen, the iPhone 6 Plus became nonfunctional but that is NOT the fault of the product in any way. Everything an experienced expert needs is provided. Instructions are a bit unclear due to translation challenges, we believe. We resorted to a recommended video to augment the printed instructions. Even though we followed instruction carefully step by step, and were successful in replacing the screen, some step was not done correctly. OUR EARNEST advice is this, The operation of replacing the screen is not a DIY project. It takes experience to overcome those steps that do not go as smoothly or easily as the instructions say or as multitude of video seem to demonstrate. There will be something that is not exactly the way it is presented and there will be some connection that will not be able to be removed and replaced as easily as one is led to believe. Again, there is nothing wrong with this product. There are a couple of things better than any video showed but the overall procedure requires some expertise we did not have - obviously, since we now have an iPhone 8 Plus and the 6 Plus is simply a repository of data for us to collect through a WiFi connection if necessary.

Update to 3 stars Finally figured out how to get the machine working consistently again. 1st bought a new metal filter, the new design has a removable part so it no longer traps water inside. This did not fix the pressure problem, just the cleanliness problem. However, I started using a thumbtack to clean the drip point in the metal cup that holds the coffee. This aha moment did not come from customer care but has taken care of the problem. Originally I had this at 5 stars for making great cappuccinos. Went down to 1 star when it stopped working more than 50% of the time. Bringing it up to 3 stars as the machine seems good, but the experience with Customer Care and having to figure out how to get it working right was not awesome. Original review: Good: When it works it makes great espresso and cappuccinos. It is easy to clean, although the sealed metal filters that came with the machine would retain water. Bad: After a 9 months the pressure was insufficient to get the double shot to go thru. No change in coffee brand. Ugly: Spoke with their customer care several times, and it seemed more like they wanted to get me not to submit a claim against the warranty than to help. Just because it made 1 cup 1 time, does not mean it wasn't failing 95% of the times. I still don't know what's wrong with the machine, if it is fixable or not, but now its outside of warranty. Would not recommend.

I don't usually leave reviews, but I felt it was important to share my opinion on this here product. I've had it for about 2 weeks now and have tested it with real golf clubs outside and inside on a big TV. First, using it indoors with the practice club that comes with the device takes some getting used to. Pairing it with my phone was a breeze, and it only took me about 2 minutes to get it all set up. It's real user friendly.

Now, as far as the true yardages go indoors with the practice club, it's a bit off. The practice club is weighted like a 7 iron, and my normal 7 iron carries in the air about 158 yards with a regular swing. With the practice club inside, I average 128 yards, which is quite different from my true yardage. The device does seem to be accurate on ball flight when it comes to open or closed face.

Moving on to real clubs, my 7 iron average is 158 yards, but with the device on my real club, it shows an average of 141 yards – closer, but still a pretty big gap. For my driver, my average drive carry is around 240 to 250 yards, but the device shows it at 216 carry. Again, the ball flight with both clubs and practice club seems accurate.

In summary, it's a fun gadget that provides some feedback on club face angle and at least gets you swinging a club. It's especially nice for nighttime or weekends when you can't go play a few holes. I would've given it 5 stars if the yardages were more accurate. However, considering the price and entertainment value, I'm satisfied with it for what I'm looking for. Hopefully, this helps others decide where to spend their hard-earned cash.

This here is a good cart for people who need wheels that turn in the front. I am in a wheelchair and I can't use carts with locked wheels anymore. When you get it, check that you have everything you need. Mine came with the smaller wheels already in place. Now, for the tricky part: (1) put the rod through the back (2) put one cotter pin and one washer on the inside (3) then put the washer, the spring, the wheel, and the other cotter pin on the outside of the cart. The cotter pin is the funny looking skinny thing. Only three of my "caps" fit, but as long as you twist those cotter pins around in different directions to lock the wheel in place - do this to all four cotter pins. Hope this helps. I found that when you fold it, the little wheels get in the way. They have to be facing back toward the big wheels and then it will fold easily. Just experiment a little. Other than that, it seems sturdy enough for a few years of traveling the Boston streets. I don't think it will last more than 3 or 4 years but that's a good estimate for rough streets.

What I enjoyed about this book wasn’t so much the story as the messaged behind the story. Why do we as women become so trusting of people in revered positions? Fathers, priests, professors? Samantha is young and beautiful and the next in line of attractive Professor Peter Bridges conquests, but like all women, she thinks she’s ‘the one’. His physical appeal, wealth, knowledge and sophistication blinds her to the real man behind the mask he wears. He is a serial abuser of women. Even his act of seduction from the moment she meets him is a well-practiced pattern of behaviour. When you have doubt, even if it 1%, don’t ignore it. Why would he, the charming professor choose her? Why is he insistent (definitely OCD) or pouring them each red wine, each evening. Is she looking for a figure to replace her philandering father who left her mother for a woman his daughter’s age? Is she taken in by his better version of herself? When she falls pregnant 2 months into their relationship, her senses become more awakened and after the birth of their daughter Emily, a maturity develops in her character. She becomes aware of his various manipulations, lies, and cruelty of other women, and, over time befriends them. The leopard doesn’t change his spots. Once a liar always a liar. Revenge is sweet. Hell hath no fury like a woman scorned. All of these are present in this tale.

I enjoy using cast iron for a lot of my cooking and grilling. I have quite a few pieces from old companies such as Griswold to new stuff from Lodge. So I wanted a baking pan in cast iron as well. But Lodge doesn't make one and from my searching very few do. So I pulled the trigger on this. First impressions were " hmm,. not bad"-- BUT-- This item is NOT the quality of a Lodge or Griswold- casting is rough, unfinished, extremely dirty and totally unacceptable to use out of the box. The "seasoned" baking pan I received had so much questionable black gunk on it, I took some coarse emery paper to the whole inside of the pan. I spent a good hour hand sanding down to bare metal and was shocked at how much black unknown material came off ( about a 3rd of a cup). After seasoning it was safe to use. If you do purchase this be prepared- old clothes and rubber gloves. You will end up with this all over you when sanding- better yet I should have taken this over to my buddies house and just sandblasted it clean. It is NOT ready to use out of the box. In hindsight is it worth it ? Depends on how much work you want to put into it - plus the original cost. Only you can decide. I would have given it more stars if it was ready to use and finished better.

Alright, so I read another review that mentioned this charger can only work with one device at a time, but I gotta say, that's not quite right. When I got this bad boy, I plugged my Acer Switch 5 into the USB-C port and it charged super quick, which was pretty awesome. After that, I hooked up my Galaxy S8 to the quick charge port and it got recognized as fast charging, so that was cool too! But then, I tried to add another phone to the USB-A smart port, and guess what? My tablet stopped charging... I unplugged the USB-A and the tablet started charging again. So, turns out the USB-A ports can't be used with the USB-C charging port... 

So if you're thinking about buying this charger, just know that you can only use 2 ports, or the 3 USB-A ports. Honestly, spending money on this for the USB-A ports ain't really worth it, but if you want it for the USB-C and quick charge port, then maybe it's not too bad, which is why I'm giving it two stars. It also comes with a USB-C to USB-C cable, which is pretty nice, since others in this price range, or even higher, don't have that. 

But here's the thing, you don't really get what you pay for, 'cause those 3 USB-A ports are basically useless and it doesn't say that anywhere in the description. In fact, it specifically says "Use it to charge a USB-C and 4 USB-powered devices simultaneously at home or in the office." I was gonna give it 3 stars since it's kinda worth it for the 2 ports and the price, but after seeing that misleading description, I gotta drop it down to 2 stars.

I bought this because I needed wheels that turned in the front - I am wheelchair bound and locked wheels are not for me anymore. When you get it, make sure you have all the pieces; mine came with the smaller wheels already inserted; NOW -- as for that rod and springs etc -- (1) put the rod thru the back (2) one cotter pin and one washer go on the inside (3) then the washer, the spring, the wheel and then the other cotter pin go outside the cart. The cotter pin is the funny looking skinny thing. Only three of my "caps" fit, but as long as you have twisted those cotter pins (you need a pair of needle nose pliers to separate the small part from the big part) and then twist them around in different directions to lock the wheel in place - do this to all four cotter pins. Hope this helps. I find that when it is folding, the little wheels sort of get in the way. They have to be facing back toward the big wheels and then it will fold easily. Just experiment a little. Other than that, it seems sturdy enough for a few years of traveling the Boston streets. I don't think it will last more than 3 or 4 years but I think that's a good estimation for rough streets.

Great large beach chair, a little higher off the ground than most, making it easier to get out of. I bought the blue/green striped pattern which is as pictured. Would be nice to have a small zippered waterproof pocket attached under the arm of the chair for phone, keys etc. It is a little hard to close, I struggle every time and haven’t figured out the secret! Nice large pouch on the back for towel etc however the flap does not secure tightly so things will fall out if you don’t carry it upright. My big issue with the chair is comfort, or lack of comfort!, while carrying it. I purchased the backpack chair to wear while riding my bike 1 mile to the beach. There is a bar on the chair that hits right across my backbone and is extreamly uncomfortable while on my bike. Luckily the ride is short! Overall the chair itself is nice, but design is not conducive to carrying comfort.

I recently got two of these Drift roses - one coral and one apricot. To my dismay, both plants arrived in a disheveled state, with no leaves whatsoever! There was just a smidgen of growth on the tip of a single stalk. The soil they were planted in was so drenched that I was genuinely worried about root rot if they'd spent one more day at the post office.

Now, I'll give credit where it's due - the two lonely leaves on each plant did appear healthy. But, it's going to be a long and arduous journey for these plants to regain their former glory. And even after they bounce back, it'll take some more time before they start blooming. So, be prepared for a bit of a DIY project with these roses.

These are definitely not the kind of plants you'd gift someone or use as a starting point for your gardening adventures. You'd be much better off heading to your local nursery or garden center for that. I'm a huge fan of Drift roses as they thrive in container gardens under Florida's hot and humid climate, but they're hard to find locally, so I resort to ordering them online.

In my eight years of gardening and ordering numerous plants online, I must say that these four Drift roses (coral, peach, apricot, and popcorn) have arrived in the most pitiful condition. However, my previous two Drift roses did make a comeback within two to three months, and I simply adore them. So, I decided to add the coral and peach varieties to my collection as well.

The first two looked like they had been scorched, while these new ones arrived completely bald. None of the four were in good shape upon arrival. But, like I mentioned earlier, with some tender loving care, a prompt repotting (get them out of that soggy soil and plastic container ASAP!), and a bit of patience, Drift roses have a knack for bouncing back.

Just be prepared for some hands-on work when they arrive - don't let them sit in the box for days on end!

been using regularly (daily since summer) a brass wand roommate found at a ross dress for less. that one had a metal valve dial to open and close the water stream to the nozzle. this was fine for awhile but after a lot of flexing of my index and middle fingers to spray paint a bunch of furniture, twisting the dial on and off as i moved thruout the yard became truly taxing on my battered nerve endings and digit muscles. i was so excited to get this new wand i couldn’t even wait until the weekend to go install it on my new hose. it’s fantastic! while i would have preferred more of a full spectrum of water release thru the handle, i am ok with the click setting - it’s extremely sensitive toward shut off so you never have to worry about overwatering. the fixture is good though i added a brass connector to increase the distance between the handle cushion and the joining hose since my hose has a shut off valve that was too close to the mouth leading to the dial being jammed shut by the cushion. the ratcheting head gives you lots of control over your spray and the wand length is just right. even though it seems really durable and sturdy, it is lightweight, so hoping for less wrist strain raising wand to water. time will tell whether it’s crafted to endure weather, water pressure stress and regular handling, but i’m hoping it holds up because i’m really happy with this wand so far!

I just got this humidifier a few days ago and so far, I'm pretty happy with it. First off, it's way quieter than any other humidifier I've owned, even on the highest fan setting. I don't understand why some reviews say it's noisy. Second, setting it up was a breeze. There aren't too many parts to deal with, which is a relief. That being said, I have to agree with other reviews that filling the tanks is a bit awkward. The tanks won't stand on their own on the side that needs to be filled, so you can't just fill and cap them in a tub like with other models. Third, I'm not sure how long the filter is going to last. It doesn't look like it'll make it through the whole winter season, but we'll see. It's frustrating that most manufacturers have moved away from metal filters with clay coatings, but I guess that's just so they can sell more filters. Finally, the tanks aren't clear, so you can't tell when they're getting low on water. It's a shame because that's a basic feature that most humidifiers have. I can't give this product five stars because of the awkwardness of filling the tanks and the inability to see when they're low on water, but the quietness and ease of assembly are definitely pluses.

We recently had our 10 month old Labrador Retriever neutered and came home from the vet with a standard clear plastic cone. It didn't even last a week before it started to crack and fall apart. Not to mention that it really hurt when the cone hit your legs as the dog tried to pass you in a room. We ultimately purchased this style cone and it worked very well with just one flaw. The cover on this style is excellent as it prevents the dog from puncturing the blow up donut inside. There is a velcro type strap that crosses the opening and secures the donut securely. It makes it adjustable to fit a range of size in dogs necks. The problem was that the black strap was not strong enough. The pup probably did chew on it a bit when the donut rotated so the strap was under his chin. I did have to sew and reinforce the strap three different times. So, I wish that it had a stronger strap, but overall the design was excellent and kept the pup from reaching areas he wasn't supposed to scratch. It was very comfortable for the dog and he liked having that pillow to lay on all the time. :) I would highly recommend it.

I got this Maidenform shapewear with high hopes, but it didn't quite meet my expectations. Let me start with the good: the color is great and the lace detail is a nice touch. The control is just right, not too tight, and it doesn't give me any back rolls like some other partial shapewear does. However, the biggest letdown is the lack of support in the bra cup area. As someone with larger boobs, I need more reinforcement than this garment provides. The cup fabric is too thin and sheer, so I wouldn't recommend wearing it under a white top or anything too revealing. It's a shame because I wanted a one-piece to avoid the bra/back roll situation, but this shapewear just doesn't cut it. Maidenform should know better, especially since they're in the business of making bras. It reminds me of a trainer I wore when I was a kid - not something I want to wear as an adult. I'll have to try wearing it with a bra for the coverage and support I need, but that defeats the whole purpose of buying a one-piece shapewear. Overall, it's disappointing.

Let's start with what I like: The headphones are very comfortable, they fit my head quite well and my ears have not gotten sore from wearing them for extended periods of time (1-2 hours). The sounds quality is good. I do not consider myself an audiophile but I can tell lousy from decent when it comes to headphones and these fit squarely in the decent category, Cons: There is a severe delay when using Bluetooth (1-2 seconds) so much so that I gave up on using the bluetooth. I just plug them in using the USB-C to 1/8" cable. It makes watching movies using Bluetooth a no-go with these headphones. I also notice the delay when pausing music. There is a 1-2 second lag from when I hit the pause button to when music actually stops. Noise cancelling doesn't do much more than add white noise to the audio. Build quality is mediocre. I have owned these 8 months and the power button broke (it is stuck depressed so I can no longer turn the headphones on). I wasn't expecting these to be awesome, but losing the Bluetooth functionality completely after 8 months seems pretty bad. The padding is also coming loose as shown in the photo. I would recommend these as a decent pair of wired headphones, but look elsewhere if you want wireless.

I had to rely on the product photos to put it together. After handling the shelves, my hands were covered in splinters and were very red and itchy, despite repeated washing.
